title: 2003 AMC 10B Problem 19
statement: Three semicircles of radius \(1\) are constructed on diameter \(\overline{AB}\) of a semicircle of radius \(2.\) The centers of the small semicircles divide \(\overline{AB}\) into four line segments of equal length, as shown. What is the area of the shaded region that lies within the large semicircle but outside the smaller semicircles?

solutions.text:
The large semicircle has area \(\dfrac12 \pi (2)^2 = 2\pi.\)

Removing the small semicircles deletes a region equal to five congruent \(60^\circ\) sectors of radius \(1\) plus two equilateral triangles of side \(1.\) Each sector has area \(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\) and each triangle has area \(\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}.\)

The shaded area is \[ \begin{gathered} 2\pi - 5 \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{6} - 2 \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt3}{4} \\ = \dfrac{7}{6}\pi - \dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}. \end{gathered} \]

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Start with the large semicircle’s area \(\tfrac12 \pi (2)^2 = 2\pi\)
The overlaps of adjacent small semicircles are \(60^\circ\) sectors plus equilateral triangles
